description: §38.1 PRECEDENCE — `<page>` → nested `<program name="w">` → `<channel>`. Two placement conditions hold at once (there is a `<page>` ancestor AND an extracted nested `<program>` ancestor) and exactly ONE code fires: E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-NESTED-PROGRAM. E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-PAGE must NOT fire. This is the S353-bryan ruling, option (b): a nested `<program>` is a FRESH placement scope, so the enclosing `<page>` is invisible to the check. It is also the right diagnostic on the merits — the nested-program code names the reason the declaration cannot be built at all (the subtree is extracted before server emission, so the WebSocket route of §38.8 is never emitted), whereas the `<page>` remedy would send the author to move a declaration out of a `<page>` that is not the problem.
rationale: §38.2 normative (S356): "A nested `<program>` SHALL be a fresh `<channel>` placement scope: an enclosing `<page>` SHALL NOT disqualify a `<channel>` declared inside a nested `<program>` … Concretely: `<page>` → `<program name=\"w\">` → `<channel>` SHALL emit E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-NESTED-PROGRAM and SHALL NOT emit E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-PAGE." §4.12.1 supplies the ground: a nested `<program>` "SHALL be subject to the same grammar rules as a top-level `<program>`" and "SHALL be a separate compilation unit", so the `<page>` is as invisible to the placement check as the parent's bindings are under §4.12.1 shared-nothing isolation.
